title: Flat split neighbourhood in Gabber's finite algebra argument
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings, B a finite A-algebra [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and I an ideal of A (no Jacobson hypothesis). Let B1 and B2 be A/I-algebras, and e: B/IB ≃ B1 × B2 a structure-map-compatible ring equivalence. Assume A/I → B1 is surjective and b in B maps to (1,0). There exist a commutative A-algebra C in the universe of A, flat over A, and a structure-map-compatible equivalence A/I ≃ C/IC. In T = C tensor_A B there are ideals K,L with K ∩ L = 0 and a scalar a in IC such that 1 tensor b - 1 - a belongs to K and 1 tensor b belongs to L + (IC)T.

source.place: Tag 0EM0, proof of lemma-helper-finite, lifting the idempotent and splitting factors

proof.text: The residue class of b is idempotent because e sends it to (1,0). Finiteness supplies integrality. Apply the existing etale idempotent lift and transport its tensor quotient equivalence along the tensor commutor to T=D tensor_A B.

For each t in T, choose a scalar whose reduction has the same first coordinate using A/I -> B1 surjective. The residual has first coordinate zero, hence multiplying it by 1-epsilon does not change its reduction. Consequently t minus that scalar belongs to (1-epsilon)+JT. Apply the finite tensor factor localization theorem.
Compose the quotient equivalences on representatives. The etale map A -> D is flat, and the localized map D -> C is flat, hence A -> C is flat.

Transport epsilon and the relation 1 tensor b-epsilon in JT to C tensor_A B. Let K=(1-epsilon_C), L=(epsilon_C). Complementary idempotents give an injective pair of quotient maps, so K intersect L is zero. The relation gives x-1 in K+IC*T and x in L+IC*T. Surjectivity C -> T/K makes the extended ideal an actual image of IC; lift the image of x-1 to a in IC. Its equality in T/K gives x-1-a in K.

theorem exists_flat_split_gabber_neighbourhood
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [Module.Finite A B] (I : Ideal A)
    (B₁ : Type w) (B₂ : Type z) [CommRing B₁] [CommRing B₂]
    [Algebra (A ⧸ I) B₁] [Algebra (A ⧸ I) B₂]
    (e : (B ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A B)) ≃+* (B₁ × B₂))
    (he : ∀ a : A, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A B)) (algebraMap A B a)) =
      (algebraMap (A ⧸ I) B₁ (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a),
        algebraMap (A ⧸ I) B₂ (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a)))
    (h₁ : Function.Surjective (algebraMap (A ⧸ I) B₁))
    (b : B) (hb : e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A B)) b) = (1, 0)) :
    ∃ (C : CommRingCat.{u}) (f : A →+* C),
      letI : Algebra A C := f.toAlgebra
      Module.Flat A C ∧
        ∃ α : A ⧸ I ≃+* C ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A C),
          (∀ a : A, α (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a) =
            Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap A C a)) ∧
          ∃ K L : Ideal (TensorProduct A C B), K ⊓ L = ⊥ ∧
            ∃ a : C, a ∈ I.map (algebraMap A C) ∧
              ((1 : C) ⊗ₜ[A] b) - 1 - algebraMap C (TensorProduct A C B) a ∈ K ∧
              ((1 : C) ⊗ₜ[A] b) ∈ L ⊔
                (I.map (algebraMap A C)).map (algebraMap C (TensorProduct A C B))
